# prismaNamespaceBrowser.ts Explained

This file is generated by Prisma, so do not edit it directly. Prisma can replace it when you regenerate the client.

Use this guide to understand what each line or small group of lines does.

```ts
/* !!! This is code generated by Prisma. Do not edit directly. !!! */
```
Prisma created this file automatically. Manual changes can be lost.

```ts
/* eslint-disable */
```
Turns off ESLint checks for this generated file.

```ts
// biome-ignore-all lint: generated file
```
Tells Biome to ignore lint warnings because this is generated code.

```ts
// @ts-nocheck
```
Tells TypeScript not to type-check this generated file.

```ts
/*
 * WARNING: This is an internal file that is subject to change!
 *
 * Under no circumstances should you import this file directly!
 *
 * All exports from this file are wrapped under a `Prisma` namespace object in the browser.ts file.
 * While this enables partial backward compatibility, it is not part of the stable public API.
 *
 * If you are looking for your Models, Enums, and Input Types, please import them from the respective
 * model files in the `model` directory!
 */
```
This warning means the file is for Prisma's internal use. Your app should import from Prisma's public generated files instead.

```ts
import * as runtime from "@prisma/client/runtime/index-browser"
```
Imports Prisma's browser runtime helpers and stores them in the `runtime` object.

```ts
export type * from '../models.js'
```
Re-exports all TypeScript types from the generated Prisma models file.

```ts
export type * from './prismaNamespace.js'
```
Re-exports Prisma namespace types from another generated internal file.

```ts
export const Decimal = runtime.Decimal
```
Exports Prisma's `Decimal` helper for precise decimal numbers.

```ts
export const NullTypes = {
```
Starts an object that groups Prisma's special null types.

```ts
  DbNull: runtime.NullTypes.DbNull as (new (secret: never) => typeof runtime.DbNull),
```
Defines `DbNull`, which means the database value is SQL `NULL`.

```ts
  JsonNull: runtime.NullTypes.JsonNull as (new (secret: never) => typeof runtime.JsonNull),
```
Defines `JsonNull`, which means the value inside a JSON field is JSON `null`.

```ts
  AnyNull: runtime.NullTypes.AnyNull as (new (secret: never) => typeof runtime.AnyNull),
```
Defines `AnyNull`, which can match either database `NULL` or JSON `null`.

```ts
}
```
Ends the `NullTypes` object.

```ts
/**
 * Helper for filtering JSON entries that have `null` on the database (empty on the db)
 *
 * @see https://www.prisma.io/docs/concepts/components/prisma-client/working-with-fields#filtering-on-a-json-field
 */
export const DbNull = runtime.DbNull
```
Exports `DbNull` so Prisma queries can filter for database-level null values.

```ts
/**
 * Helper for filtering JSON entries that have JSON `null` values (not empty on the db)
 *
 * @see https://www.prisma.io/docs/concepts/components/prisma-client/working-with-fields#filtering-on-a-json-field
 */
export const JsonNull = runtime.JsonNull
```
Exports `JsonNull` so Prisma queries can filter for JSON fields that contain JSON `null`.

```ts
/**
 * Helper for filtering JSON entries that are `Prisma.DbNull` or `Prisma.JsonNull`
 *
 * @see https://www.prisma.io/docs/concepts/components/prisma-client/working-with-fields#filtering-on-a-json-field
 */
export const AnyNull = runtime.AnyNull
```
Exports `AnyNull` so Prisma queries can match either kind of null value.

```ts
export const TransactionIsolationLevel = runtime.makeStrictEnum({
```
Creates a strict enum for database transaction isolation levels.

```ts
  ReadUncommitted: 'ReadUncommitted',
```
Allows reading data that other transactions have not committed yet.

```ts
  ReadCommitted: 'ReadCommitted',
```
Allows reading only data that has already been committed.

```ts
  RepeatableRead: 'RepeatableRead',
```
Keeps reads consistent during a transaction.

```ts
  Serializable: 'Serializable'
```
Uses the strictest transaction behavior, making transactions behave as if they run one at a time.

```ts
} as const)
```
Ends the enum object and preserves exact string values.

```ts
export type TransactionIsolationLevel = (typeof TransactionIsolationLevel)[keyof typeof TransactionIsolationLevel]
```
Creates a TypeScript type from the transaction isolation enum values.
